z: 瑁 indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Gossip is how a house talks about its own when they have left the room. Healing speech waits until they are back, and then says the hard thing to the face, cleanly.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑁 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Tell one story tonight in which a person in this house is repaired, not mocked.

z: 瑃 indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Across the old writings, the warning against scoffing is constant. A scoffer cannot be taught, and a house that scoffs cannot learn itself.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑃 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 瑄 indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Some truths are not ready for speech. Presence holds them without using them as a weapon. A weaponized silence is still a weapon.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑄 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Be findable. Tell the house which room you will be in, and be in it.

z: 瑆 indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A child who watches a break become a lifelong trial learns that love is a court. A child who watches a break become a mended bowl learns that love can survive its own failure.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑆 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 瑇 indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu
line:
Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is indlala yomphimbo, indlala, izindlala ezincane zomphimbo, izindlala, umgudu womoya, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑇 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

z: 瑋 ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The sciences of a lasting household call this resilience. The older word is faithfulness. It does not deny the dark. It refuses to let the dark be the only speaker.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑋 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 瑍 ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Many sacred traditions, in different grammars, say the same hard thing: the injury stops when someone declines to pass it on. This is not weakness. It is the end of a chain.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑍 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 瑒 ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
At the table, anger wants the last word. The last word is rarely food. Let the sentence end before it becomes the story the children will tell about this house.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑒 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 瑓 ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑓 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 瑕 ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
What you wish were yours, name it exactly, in the hearing of the person who has it. Then do not reach. The naming is the confession. The not-reaching is the turn.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑕 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Say out loud, in the hearing of the person, the exact good you wished were yours. Then leave it theirs.

z: 瑗 ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Name the loss you are counting. Often it is a person in the room, not a disaster outside. Then put your body beside that person. That is the whole practice.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑗 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 瑙 ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Give before you calculate whether you will be thanked. Thanks are not the food. If you require them, you have made a trade, and a trade is not yet a family.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokudla. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑙 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

z: 瑚 ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Wisdom is not silence forever. There is a time to speak. The test is whether the words can be repeated in front of the person, and still be a kindness.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑚 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 瑛 ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Look at the work you have stopped seeing. Name it. The naming is not flattery. It is the return of sight, and sight is the turn.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑛 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Look at one ordinary object they mended or prepared, and say what it cost them.

z: 瑜 ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to be interesting. You do have to be in the house.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑜 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 瑝 ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Accountability is the first half. Without it, forgiveness is a fog. The one who broke the trust says what was done, without a speech about why it was almost justified.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑝 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 瑞 ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑞 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Bring food. Take the lower seat. Stay past the moment you become uncomfortable.

z: 瑟 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Despair often tells the truth about pain and then adds a lie about forever. Keep the truth. Decline the forever. Forever is not a fact available to a person at a window.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑟 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 瑠 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Accountability remains. Mercy is not the cancellation of truth. It is the decision that truth will not be used as a knife at breakfast for the next twenty years.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑠 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 瑢 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who has turned anger into protection does not become mild. The wall is still warm. What changes is the face it turns toward. It faces the street, not the cradle.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑢 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 瑣 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's dignity is not the right to be obeyed in every small thing. It is the right to be respected while still listening. The listening is what makes the respect true.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑣 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

z: 瑤 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across generations, envy of the young is fear of being finished. Admiration of the young is how an elder stays in the story without owning it.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑤 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Ask the person to show you how they did the thing. Be a student for ten minutes.

z: 瑩 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who has been afraid and stayed is a better teacher than an elder who claims never to have shaken. The shaking, survived, is the lesson.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑩 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 瑪 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who gives the best piece away is not being careless with the future. The elder is showing the future how a house continues.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑪 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Feed the guest, or the youngest, before you take your own share.

z: 瑫 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's stories are a kind of speech that builds or bends a family. Tell the story in which people are repaired. The other story will tell itself.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑫 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Say the hard thing to the face, once, cleanly, with no audience.

z: 瑭 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who still notices the small faithfulness in the house is a gift to the young. The young become what is noticed.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑭 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Remove the sneer from a sentence and speak it again. Notice how much of it was only the sneer.

z: 瑯 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder's quiet can be a shelter or a locked door. The young can tell which, by whether they are welcome to come and say nothing beside you.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑯 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Sit with a person who is not ready to speak. Let ten minutes pass without fixing them.

z: 瑰 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Some breaks end a household. That too can be told with dignity. Forgiveness then is the refusal to poison the years that follow. The children still have to live in them.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑰 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 瑱 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder who speaks of the dead by name, without recruiting the young into despair, gives the family its memory and its future in the same breath.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑱 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

z: 瑳 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who has looked again, many mornings, is a quiet argument against the lie. Do not turn the elder into a slogan. Let the morning itself be seen.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑳 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 瑶 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who lays down a feud gives the young a future that is not already written. That is one of the last great gifts a generation can give the next.

This is the work of a house after a loss. The member drawn is ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 瑶 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: If a child is carrying a feud that belongs to adults, take it back. Say that it is not theirs.

z: 瑾 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Anger is the house defending itself before it has measured the threat. Left alone, it burns the people it meant to keep. The heat is not the enemy. Direction is. Turned, the same heat stands in the doorway so the small ones can sleep.

This is the work of a house after a loss. ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 瑾 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Teach the strong child to stand in front of the smaller one. That is anger, turned, and it can be learned young.

z: 璁 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Pride needs an audience and a person beneath it. Dignity needs neither. Hidden inside pride is the refusal to be nothing. That refusal is good. It becomes poison only when someone else must be smaller for it to stand.

This is the work of a house after a loss. ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 璁 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Praise a person in the house for a quality you do not share. Do not add a correction.

z: 璃 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Envy is love of a good thing, twisted until the good thing must shrink. The love was real. That is why it hurts. Turned, the same look becomes admiration, which is fed by another person's light.

This is the work of a house after a loss. ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 璃 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: When a sibling is praised, add one true sentence of your own. Do not balance it with your own news.

z: 璅 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear is the mind counting what it loves and what it could lose. That count is not a defect. It is proof of attachment, and attachment is how a family exists. Courage is fear that stays in the room.

This is the work of a house after a loss. ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 璅 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 璆 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Greed is the fear that there will not be enough, wearing the mask of appetite. Bread kept in a closed hand goes stale. Generosity is the same hand remembering the table.

This is the work of a house after a loss. ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 璆 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

z: 璇 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The tongue is the smallest member and the widest fire. Every tradition that lasted put a guard on it, because a family is made of sentences more than of walls.

This is the work of a house after a loss. ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 璇 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 璈 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu
line:
Contempt is a shortcut. It saves a person from having to look. Inside it is the power it refuses: the power to see a thing clearly. Clear sight is the beginning of thanks.

This is the work of a house after a loss. ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 璈 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Thank a person for a labor you have stopped seeing. Thank the labor, not their temperament.

z: 璉 indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
There is a silence that punishes and a silence that accompanies. They use the same closed mouth. The difference is whether the person has left while remaining in the chair.

This is the work of a house after a loss. indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 璉 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to perform a talk.

z: 璋 indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Betrayal proves that trust was real, because only a real bond breaks with that sound. Forgiveness is not the pretence that the bowl never cracked. It is gold in the crack, and the decision to eat from that bowl again, slowly.

This is the work of a house after a loss. indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 璋 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Name the break once, without extra charges. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and repeat it tomorrow.

z: 璐 indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Grief is love with nowhere to go. It feels like an evil because it stops the house. It is not an invader. It is a force large enough to be mistaken for one. Compassion is that force sitting down beside someone else.

This is the work of a house after a loss. indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 璐 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Do not hurry a grieving person into cheer. Let the absent name be said.

z: 璒 indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Despair says the dawn is a lie because the room is dark. The force inside it is the fact that someone is still at the window. Waiting is already a kind of faithfulness, even when it feels like defeat.

This is the work of a house after a loss. indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 璒 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 璗 indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Revenge believes that pain can be balanced by being copied. It cannot. The copy multiplies, and the family becomes a ledger. Mercy is the refusal to become the injury.

This is the work of a house after a loss. indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 璗 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 璘 indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
A marriage can survive a true no. It cannot survive a no that was only a wound looking for a second body. Protection is the no that guards the bond, not the no that wins the evening.

This is the work of a house after a loss. indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 璘 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 璙 indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
A parent who comes down to a child's height does not lose rank. Rank was the costume. The person remains. Dignity is the choice to be seen without requiring worship.

This is the work of a house after a loss. indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 璙 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Admit one small wrong without a speech about your intentions. Stop when the admission is complete.

z: 璜 indlala yomzimba osemncane, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A family that can clap for its own is already rich. The eye is the first thief, and it can be the first blessing. The difference is whether the good is allowed to remain in the other hand.

Brothers and sisters are the first public. What you do to be admired at home becomes the way they will treat their own children. Give them a dignity they can copy.

The teachings that endured all warn the eye. They also bless the eye that rejoices. Rejoicing is not a mood. It is a decision made again each time the other person shines.

Psychology is simple here. The closed hand teaches the body that the world is about to run out. The open hand teaches it that tomorrow includes other people.

Gossip is how a house talks about its own when they have left the room. Healing speech waits until they are back, and then says the hard thing to the face, cleanly.

line:
Across the old writings, the warning against scoffing is constant. A scoffer cannot be taught, and a house that scoffs cannot learn itself.

z: 甍 i-ovari, ingqe, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Some truths are not ready for speech. Presence holds them without using them as a weapon. A weaponized silence is still a weapon.

z: 甎 i-ovari, ingqe, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu

A child who watches a break become a lifelong trial learns that love is a court. A child who watches a break become a mended bowl learns that love can survive its own failure.

z: 甑 i-ovari, ingqe, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

practice: Bring food. Take the lower seat. Stay past the moment you become uncomfortable.

z: 甓 i-ovari, ingqe, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
The sciences of a lasting household call this resilience. The older word is faithfulness. It does not deny the dark. It refuses to let the dark be the only speaker.

z: 甕 i-ovari, ingqe, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu

Many sacred traditions, in different grammars, say the same hard thing: the injury stops when someone declines to pass it on. This is not weakness. It is the end of a chain.

practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 甗 i-ovari, ingqe, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu
line:
At the table, anger wants the last word. The last word is rarely food. Let the sentence end before it becomes the story the children will tell about this house.

line:
The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

z: 甚 isibeletho, ama-ovari, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
What you wish were yours, name it exactly, in the hearing of the person who has it. Then do not reach. The naming is the confession. The not-reaching is the turn.

z: 甜 isibeletho, ama-ovari, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Name the loss you are counting. Often it is a person in the room, not a disaster outside. Then put your body beside that person. That is the whole practice.

practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 甞 isibeletho, ama-ovari, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Give before you calculate whether you will be thanked. Thanks are not the food. If you require them, you have made a trade, and a trade is not yet a family.

Wisdom is not silence forever. There is a time to speak. The test is whether the words can be repeated in front of the person, and still be a kindness.

line:
Look at the work you have stopped seeing. Name it. The naming is not flattery. It is the return of sight, and sight is the turn.

z: 甥 isibeletho, ama-ovari, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to be interesting. You do have to be in the house.

z: 甦 isibeletho, ama-ovari, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Accountability is the first half. Without it, forgiveness is a fog. The one who broke the trust says what was done, without a speech about why it was almost justified.

practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 用 isibeletho, ama-ovari, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu

The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

line:
Despair often tells the truth about pain and then adds a lie about forever. Keep the truth. Decline the forever. Forever is not a fact available to a person at a window.

practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

line:
Accountability remains. Mercy is not the cancellation of truth. It is the decision that truth will not be used as a knife at breakfast for the next twenty years.

practice: If a child is carrying a feud that belongs to adults, take it back. Say that it is not theirs.

line:
An elder who has turned anger into protection does not become mild. The wall is still warm. What changes is the face it turns toward. It faces the street, not the cradle.

practice: Teach the strong child to stand in front of the smaller one. That is anger, turned, and it can be learned young.

z: 甯 isibeletho, ama-ovari, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu

An elder's dignity is not the right to be obeyed in every small thing. It is the right to be respected while still listening. The listening is what makes the respect true.

line:
Across generations, envy of the young is fear of being finished. Admiration of the young is how an elder stays in the story without owning it.

An elder who has been afraid and stayed is a better teacher than an elder who claims never to have shaken. The shaking, survived, is the lesson.

line:
An elder who gives the best piece away is not being careless with the future. The elder is showing the future how a house continues.

line:
An elder's stories are a kind of speech that builds or bends a family. Tell the story in which people are repaired. The other story will tell itself.

line:
An elder who still notices the small faithfulness in the house is a gift to the young. The young become what is noticed.

practice: Thank a person for a labor you have stopped seeing. Thank the labor, not their temperament.

z: 町 isibeletho, ama-ovari, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder's quiet can be a shelter or a locked door. The young can tell which, by whether they are welcome to come and say nothing beside you.

line:
Some breaks end a household. That too can be told with dignity. Forgiveness then is the refusal to poison the years that follow. The children still have to live in them.

line:
An elder who speaks of the dead by name, without recruiting the young into despair, gives the family its memory and its future in the same breath.

line:
An elder who has looked again, many mornings, is a quiet argument against the lie. Do not turn the elder into a slogan. Let the morning itself be seen.

line:
An elder who lays down a feud gives the young a future that is not already written. That is one of the last great gifts a generation can give the next.

Anger is the house defending itself before it has measured the threat. Left alone, it burns the people it meant to keep. The heat is not the enemy. Direction is. Turned, the same heat stands in the doorway so the small ones can sleep.

line:
Pride needs an audience and a person beneath it. Dignity needs neither. Hidden inside pride is the refusal to be nothing. That refusal is good. It becomes poison only when someone else must be smaller for it to stand.

line:
Envy is love of a good thing, twisted until the good thing must shrink. The love was real. That is why it hurts. Turned, the same look becomes admiration, which is fed by another person's light.

z: 畈 isibeletho, ama-ovari, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Fear is the mind counting what it loves and what it could lose. That count is not a defect. It is proof of attachment, and attachment is how a family exists. Courage is fear that stays in the room.

practice: Tell the truth you have been saving, and remain in the room after it is told.

z: 畉 isibeletho, ama-ovari, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Greed is the fear that there will not be enough, wearing the mask of appetite. Bread kept in a closed hand goes stale. Generosity is the same hand remembering the table.

practice: Put one thing you were keeping back into the middle of the table.

z: 畊 isibeletho, ama-ovari, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The tongue is the smallest member and the widest fire. Every tradition that lasted put a guard on it, because a family is made of sentences more than of walls.

z: 畋 isibeletho, ama-ovari, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Contempt is a shortcut. It saves a person from having to look. Inside it is the power it refuses: the power to see a thing clearly. Clear sight is the beginning of thanks.

z: 界 isibeletho, ama-ovari, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
There is a silence that punishes and a silence that accompanies. They use the same closed mouth. The difference is whether the person has left while remaining in the chair.

z: 畍 isibeletho, ama-ovari, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Betrayal proves that trust was real, because only a real bond breaks with that sound. Forgiveness is not the pretence that the bowl never cracked. It is gold in the crack, and the decision to eat from that bowl again, slowly.

z: 畎 isibeletho, ama-ovari, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu
line:
Grief is love with nowhere to go. It feels like an evil because it stops the house. It is not an invader. It is a force large enough to be mistaken for one. Compassion is that force sitting down beside someone else.

practice: Answer the ordinary request of a grieving child. Do not make them perform a sadness you recognize.

z: 畏 i-plasenta, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Despair says the dawn is a lie because the room is dark. The force inside it is the fact that someone is still at the window. Waiting is already a kind of faithfulness, even when it feels like defeat.

practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

z: 畐 i-plasenta, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Revenge believes that pain can be balanced by being copied. It cannot. The copy multiplies, and the family becomes a ledger. Mercy is the refusal to become the injury.

z: 畑 i-plasenta, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:

z: 畒 i-plasenta, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A parent who comes down to a child's height does not lose rank. Rank was the costume. The person remains. Dignity is the choice to be seen without requiring worship.

practice: Praise a person in the house for a quality you do not share. Do not add a correction.

z: 畔 i-plasenta, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A family that can clap for its own is already rich. The eye is the first thief, and it can be the first blessing. The difference is whether the good is allowed to remain in the other hand.

practice: When a sibling is praised, add one true sentence of your own. Do not balance it with your own news.

z: 留 i-plasenta, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The parent at the dark door does not stop being afraid. They stop leaving. Be with the frightened. Do not perform fearlessness. A performed bravery teaches a child to hide.

practice: Name the person you are afraid of losing, and spend the next hour near them without a speech.

z: 畚 i-plasenta, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Generosity is not the opposite of need. It is need that has remembered other mouths. The first portion, not the remainder, teaches the house what it is.

practice: Give a thing away that you still like. Do not wait until you are tired of it.

z: 畛 i-plasenta, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Healing speech is not sweetness. Sweetness can be a lie. Healing speech is accuracy with mercy. It names the hurt and refuses the insult that wanted to ride along.

practice: Tell one story tonight in which a person in this house is repaired, not mocked.

z: 畜 i-plasenta, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
What is despised at home is despised twice, because home was the place it should have been safe to be plain. Appreciation is looking that did not turn away.

practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 畝 i-plasenta, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Cold silence is absence wearing a body. Presence is that silence warmed by staying. Put the object down. Let the eyes finish the sentence the mouth is not ready to speak.

practice: Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to perform a talk.

z: 畠 i-plasenta, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
A family that cannot mend becomes a set of strangers who still share a key. Mercy here is not amnesia. It is the refusal to make the break the only story the children inherit.

practice: Name the break once, without extra charges. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and repeat it tomorrow.

z: 畢 i-plasenta, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The empty chair is not decorated away. The shawl is the theology. Every house that lasted taught its people to weep with those who weep, and only then to speak.

practice: Do not hurry a grieving person into cheer. Let the absent name be said.

z: 畤 i-plasenta, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Hope, in the old sense, is not a mood and not a forecast. It is the small fidelity of looking again. Families are made of that looking: one more morning, one more place set.

practice: Open the curtain before you decide what the day is. Let the house see you do it.

z: 略 i-plasenta, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The open hand and the cup of water do not erase the wrong. They stop the wrong from becoming the family name. The account can be told. It does not have to be continued.

practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 畦 i-plasenta, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Children learn what strength is from the body that stands between them and the weather. If that body spends itself on them, they learn that love arrives as weather. Turn the heat toward the actual danger.

practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 畧 i-plasenta, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
In a marriage, pride keeps a ledger of who apologized last. Dignity throws the ledger out and keeps the person. You can be wrong and still be whole.

practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 畩 i-plasenta, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Between spouses, envy dresses as criticism. The dress is thin. Under it is the wish to be the one who is praised. Say the praise. Leave the gift where it landed.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at i-plasenta, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 畩 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Clap, or thank, before you comment. Let the first sound from you be glad.

z: 番 i-plasenta, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
In a marriage, fear says, if I tell the truth I will be left. Courage tells the truth and remains seated. The staying is the larger sentence.

practice: Tell the truth you have been saving, and remain in the room after it is told.

z: 畫 i-plasenta, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
A marriage becomes a grievance when the store is private. What is earned may be stewarded. What is hoarded becomes a wall between two people who share a bed.

practice: Put one thing you were keeping back into the middle of the table.

z: 畬 i-plasenta, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
In a marriage, the second sentence is usually the one that only wanted to win. Speak the first, which is the truth. Keep the second. The keeping is love.

practice: If you gave someone a cruel name, retire it today, out loud, and do not use it again.

z: 畭 i-plasenta, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A marriage dies faster from sneering than from anger. Anger still believes the other person matters. Contempt has already left, and only the body remains at the table.

practice: Look at one ordinary object they mended or prepared, and say what it cost them.

z: 畯 i-plasenta, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
In a marriage, the punishing quiet can last longer than a blow, and it teaches the same lesson: you are alone in this room. Presence refuses to teach that.

practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 畱 i-plasenta, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Name the break once, plainly, without the extra charges that make you feel righteous. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and do it again tomorrow. Trust is rebuilt at that size.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at i-plasenta, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 畱 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 畲 i-plasenta, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Do not correct a grieving person into cheer. Bring food. Take the lower seat. Let the name of the absent be said. The name is how the absent remain in the family.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at i-plasenta, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 畲 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Answer the ordinary request of a grieving child. Do not make them perform a sadness you recognize.

z: 畳 i-plasenta, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Open the curtain before you decide what the day is. Let the house see you do it. The gesture is small, and it is the whole teaching.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at i-plasenta, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 畳 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

z: 畴 i-plasenta, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Do one undeserved kindness to the person you are keeping score against. Do not mention the score. The mention would turn the kindness back into a move.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at i-plasenta, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 畴 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Tell the truth of the wrong once, to the person, and then do not serve it at breakfast.

z: 當 i-plasenta, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
The counsel that lasted did not flatter rage. It asked the strong to become a wall for the weak. That is the ethic of a parent and of an elder: your size is a shelter, or it is a threat.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at i-plasenta, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 當 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If you have already burned someone you love, say so before the day ends, and then do one ordinary kindness with your hands.

z: 畷 i-plasenta, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The old wisdom is severe on the high seat. It is not severe on the upright spine. Stand up. Then let the others stand. A house of one standing person is a court, not a family.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at i-plasenta, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 畷 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

z: 畸 i-plasenta, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A child who is envied by a parent carries a weight no child can name. Admiration from above is a kind of safety. It says, your becoming does not threaten my place.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at i-plasenta, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 畸 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Ask the person to show you how they did the thing. Be a student for ten minutes.

z: 畹 i-plasenta, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
A child learns courage from a body that does not abandon the feeling. Sit until the breath slows. Explanation can wait. Presence cannot.

practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 畺 i-plasenta, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Children do not need every desire answered. They need to see a hand open. The open hand is their picture of tomorrow, and tomorrow is either a threat or a table.

practice: Give a thing away that you still like. Do not wait until you are tired of it.

z: 畽 i-plasenta, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A child believes the sentence more than the apology that follows it. Speak as if the sentence will live in them, because it will. This is not fear. It is care.

practice: Tell one story tonight in which a person in this house is repaired, not mocked.

z: 畾 i-plasenta, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu
line:
The ordinary work, the meal, the repaired hinge, the repeated story, is the curriculum of a family. Thank the labor, not the performance of being easy to live with.

practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 畿 isende, ingqe, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A child does not need a conversation performed. A child needs a person who can be found. Being findable is the practice. The words can come later, or not.

practice: Be findable. Tell the house which room you will be in, and be in it.

z: 疁 isende, ingqe, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Forgiveness does not require the betrayed to be foolish. It requires them to decide whether the person is still a member. Membership is a practice after it has been a wound.

practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 疂 isende, ingqe, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
A marriage that has lost a child, or a parent, or a future, needs presence more than explanation. Explanation is a way of leaving. Sitting is a way of staying.

practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

z: 疆 isende, ingqe, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A marriage in despair does not need a speech about gratitude. It needs one true plan for tomorrow that both people can bear. Make the plan small enough to be kept.

practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 疇 isende, ingqe, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
In a marriage, revenge is often petty and therefore easy to excuse. The small cut, repeated, is how love is replaced by a contest. Mercy is leaving one cut unanswered.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at isende, ingqe, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 疇 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 疉 isende, ingqe, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Accountability begins when you can say, the heat was mine. Wisdom begins when you can say, it had a better door. Compassion begins when the person you nearly burned is still in the room, and you stay.

This is the work of a house after a loss. Look long enough at isende, ingqe, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 疉 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 疊 isende, ingqe, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Self-reflection is the moment you notice you needed to win. Accountability is saying so before you are forced. The turn from pride to dignity is mostly this small honesty.

practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 疋 isende, ingqe, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Siblings are assigned the same story and different gifts. Envy calls this injustice. Admiration calls it a house with more than one lamp. Both lamps belong on the table.

practice: Say out loud, in the hearing of the person, the exact good you wished were yours. Then leave it theirs.

z: 疌 isende, ingqe, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Many houses, under many names, give the same command: do not be ruled by dread, and do not despise the person who is. The strong are asked to stay, not to sneer.

practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 疎 isende, ingqe, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Hospitality is the oldest sociology of the lasting house. The stranger eats first. The family that cannot do this for a guest will eventually fail to do it for itself.

practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

z: 疏 isende, ingqe, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Siblings remember the name they were called on the worst day. Do not give them that name. Give them the name of the good you have actually seen them do.

practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 疑 isende, ingqe, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Children who are met with contempt learn to hide the clumsy part, which is most of them. Appreciation gives that part a chair.

practice: Look at one ordinary object they mended or prepared, and say what it cost them.

z: 疒 isende, ingqe, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The old practice of sitting with the sick, of keeping watch, of not filling the air, is this turn. Do not rush to be useful. Be there.

practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 疔 isende, ingqe, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The wisdom shared by many houses is hard: do not let the sun go down on a break you are willing to heal, and do not call it healing if you are only waiting to retell it.

practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 疚 isende, ingqe, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Children grieve in strange hours and then ask for ordinary things. Both are grief. Answer the ordinary thing. Do not make them perform a sadness you can recognize.

practice: Bring food. Take the lower seat. Stay past the moment you become uncomfortable.

z: 疝 isende, ingqe, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A child who sees an adult look again, after a bad day, learns that a bad day is not a verdict. This is worth more than any optimism you could announce.

practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 疢 isende, ingqe, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Children are the usual casualties of a score kept between adults. They did not agree to carry it. Mercy toward the person you resent is also protection of the child.

practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 疣 isende, ingqe, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Siblings fight because they share a roof and a hunger. The fight is not the failure. The failure is when the stronger one discovers a liking for the smaller one's fear. Protection refuses that discovery.

Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

Across generations, envy of the young is fear of being finished. Admiration of the young is how an elder stays in the story without owning it.

An elder who still notices the small faithfulness in the house is a gift to the young. The young become what is noticed.

An elder who has looked again, many mornings, is a quiet argument against the lie. Do not turn the elder into a slogan. Let the morning itself be seen.
